The UNICEF/Trudell 2017 country review for Madagascar sets out the language policy, the education policy and the studies feeding the Education Sector Plan 2018-2022, and the only language-policy activity it names is a national seminar on language policy in education organised by the French embassy; it names no programme, body, start date or funding for reversing shift in Malagasy or its varieties. The UNESCO PEER Madagascar inclusion profile describes only the sector plan's reading, mother-tongue transition and plurilingual aims, and records that provision is made for adopting a new language policy. Searched: Trudell 2017 Madagascar country review; PEER Madagascar inclusion profile.

Not established from the sources consulted. The UNESCO PEER Guinea-Bissau inclusion profile names only the National Literacy and Non-Formal Education Policy's aim to develop a language policy document and to promote Portuguese, Creole and national languages as languages of education, learning and professional qualification, with no implementing body, no start date and no funding attached. Lopes, drawing on four exploratory interviews with Guinean students, treats the non-officialisation of Creole as an open question and argues the State should consider valorising it; he names no current programme. Searched: PEER Guinea-Bissau inclusion profile; Lopes, UNILAB repository.
